simple.meaning: מְרֹר (mᵉrôr) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a bitter herb.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 12:8. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְרֹר (H4844) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מְרֹר (mᵉrôr) / H4844 is traced through Exodus 12:8, Numbers 9:11, Lamentations 3:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.

timeline.evidenceText: They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
In the second month, on the fourteenth day at evening they shall keep it; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
He has filled me with bitterness.

definitions.full: H4844. maror [ מָרֹר ] noun masculine bitter thing, bitter herb (compare Late Hebrew id., bitter herb ; on form see Ba NB 194 ); — only plural מְרֹרִים Exod 12:8 ; Num 9:11 , מְרוֺרִים Lam 3:15 ; — bitter herbs , in Passover meal Exod 12:8 ; Num 9:11 (both P); compare בַּמּ ׳הִשְׂבִּיעַנִי Lam 3:15 , figurative of distress inflicted (|| לַעֲנָה ).
